description: Versioned lifecycle emission-factor corpus. Single source of truth for every repository that converts a fuel mix into a carbon intensity. Each record names the citekey it derives from, the exact row in the cited table, that row's published range, and, where the value departs from the cited median, a deviation block giving the reason. Citekeys resolve against docs/CITATIONS.csl.json. A record with no citekey MUST carry an `assumption` string and evidence tier E; the loader rejects anything else.

factors.note: Was 900 in carbon-lens before 2026-08-23 ('conservative; subcritical/lignite runs higher') and 820 in carbon-aware-dispatcher. Converged on the published median. The upward fudge was not justifiable: the AR5 median is already a global median across a fleet that is largely subcritical, and the same argument runs the other way for supercritical and ultra-supercritical units. Zones reporting lignite separately should map it to the `lignite` key instead of inflating this one.

factors.assumption: AR5 Annex III Table A.III.2 has no lignite row; its only coal row is the pulverised-coal (PC) row. 1050 is an assumed brown-coal/peat-class value carried over from carbon-aware-dispatcher with no source found. It is above the published maximum of the PC coal range (910), which is plausible for lignite but is not evidenced here. Two leads exist, neither confirmed by this project: the companion audit in carbon-aware-dispatcher notes that the German Federal Environment Agency publishes 1054 for Braunkohle (UBA CLIMATE CHANGE 35/2021, Tabelle 98), and that 1050 is exactly the midpoint of the 800-1300 lignite range in Turconi et al. (2013); it is also Turconi's upper bound for hard coal, so a derivation and a transcription slip fit equally well. Neither source was read here. Surfaced to API consumers as an assumption.
factors.note: Used only by providers that report a distinct lignite/brown-coal bucket.

Was 430 in carbon-lens before 2026-08-23 ('efficient CCGT end') and 490 in carbon-aware-dispatcher. Converged on the published median. Picking the efficient-CCGT end understated every gas-heavy zone: real fleets mix CCGT with open-cycle peakers, which are worse than the median, and the AR5 median already carries 91 gCO2eq/kWh of upstream methane.

AR5 Annex III Table A.III.2 has NO oil row; this value does not come from IPCC despite both repositories previously implying it did. The 650 traces to UK POSTnote 268 (October 2006) by way of the Electricity Maps default-factor table, and the POSTnote has now been read: it states 'The average carbon footprint of oil-fired electricity generation plants in the UK is ~650gCO2eq/kWh'. That is a 2006 UK-fleet average for a fuel supplying 1% of UK generation as peaking back-up, so it falls short of a global lifecycle median and is a materially weaker basis than every IPCC-backed row here; it is tiered C accordingly. Both repositories independently carried 650, which points to a shared upstream.
Same physical quantity as `oil`; kept as a distinct key because EIA and GridStatus report the bucket under this name. The loader asserts the two values stay equal.
Both repositories already agreed on the published median.

Both repositories already agreed on the published median. Note the published maximum is 2200: reservoir hydro in warm climates can emit two orders of magnitude above the median through methane from flooded biomass, and a single global median hides that entirely. Brazilian and Canadian reservoir zones are the ones this most plausibly misstates.

The disagreement (carbon-lens 11, carbon-aware-dispatcher 12) came down to which row to read: 11 is the onshore median, 12 the offshore median (range 8.0/12/35). Resolved to onshore, because onshore dominates the generation these providers report (EIA 2023 US net generation was 421,007 GWh onshore against 134 GWh offshore). Zones with material offshore capacity (GB, DK, DE, NL) are understated by at most 1 gCO2eq/kWh on the wind fraction, which is immaterial against the spread on every other factor here.

Was 41 in carbon-lens, commented 'utility PV median'. That comment was wrong: 41 is the ROOFTOP median (range 26/41/60); the utility median is 48. The intent recorded in the comment was right and the value did not match it, so the value was corrected rather than the comment. carbon-aware-dispatcher's 45 matches neither row and traces to the Electricity Maps default table, which lists a single rounded solar figure of 45 attributed to IPCC 2014. Utility is the correct row here because balancing-authority fuel-mix feeds report utility-scale generation; behind-the-meter rooftop does not appear in them (EIA 2023 splits 162,683 GWh utility PV from 73,406 GWh small-scale distributed PV, and only the former is in the hourly mix).
Both repositories already agreed on the published median.

The dedicated-energy-crop row; the cofiring row (620/740/890) would apply to biomass cofired with coal, so a provider reporting cofired biomass is understated by roughly 3x here. Deliberately NOT counted as renewable or carbon-free for the percentage calculations even though AR5 groups it with renewables: biogenic-CO2 accounting is contested and counting combustion as carbon-free is the more misleading of the two errors. Table A.III.2 excludes biogenic CO2 from the direct column by convention (footnote ii).
Wave and tidal. Used only by carbon-aware-dispatcher; carbon-lens has no provider reporting this bucket. Verified against the primary table while resolving the rest.

factors.assumption: AR5 Annex III Table A.III.2 has no municipal-waste row. 580 is an assumed value carried over from carbon-aware-dispatcher with no source found. Table A.III.11 in the same annex covers waste TREATMENT practices only, so it does not support a waste-to-energy electricity number. Surfaced to API consumers as an assumption.

A blended coal+gas bucket for providers (notably Grid India) that report 'thermal' without splitting it. 750 is an assumed blend and no source states it. It sits between the coal (820) and gas (490) medians and implies roughly a 79/21 coal/gas split, which is broadly consistent with India's thermal fleet but is not evidenced here. Surfaced to API consumers as an assumption.

Storage has no emission factor of its own. Battery discharge re-delivers energy that was already counted, and already attributed emissions, when it was generated, so including it in a weighted average over the fuel mix double-counts the energy. It is therefore EXCLUDED from both the numerator and the denominator rather than being given a factor. carbon-lens previously assigned it 0 AND left it in the denominator, which diluted intensity downward every time batteries discharged; its own code comment flagged that as 'not zero in reality'. carbon-aware-dispatcher already excluded storage and was right. Note that Electricity Maps instead assigns discharge the world-average intensity (301); that is a defensible alternative which attributes rather than excludes, and it needs charge-source attribution to be better than exclusion.
factors.note: value is null by design: a null value means 'no factor applies', and the loader requires storage:true for it.

factors.assumption: Same treatment and same reasoning as `battery`: pumped hydro is storage, so it is excluded from the weighted average and carries no factor.
factors.note: EIA reports this as PS. carbon-lens previously had no mapping for it at all.

factors.assumption: Catch-all for unknown, mixed and imported generation. 300 is an assumed placeholder present in both repositories with no source. It is NOT conservative in the direction the original comment claimed: if the unknown bucket is in fact thermal, 300 understates it badly. Electricity Maps assigns 700 to the comparable 'unknown' bucket on a stated assumption of thermal generation, so the plausible range for this single number spans 300 to 700. Left at 300 because there is no evidence to prefer either end, and changing it would be an unforced behavioural change; surfaced to API consumers as an assumption so the uncertainty is visible rather than implied. One lead worth recording: NESO's published UK factor table (https://api.carbonintensity.org.uk/intensity/factors) assigns its 'Other' bucket exactly 300, so this value may have been taken from there rather than assumed independently. That is unconfirmed, and NESO's table is direct-combustion rather than lifecycle, so it would not license the number on this corpus's basis even if true.
factors.note: GridStatus 'imports' also maps here, which is a second, separate weakness: imports have the exporting zone's intensity, which flow tracing computes properly for the European network.
